title: S2P S2-VS-06 VISDOMS-S PHASE A/B1
description: The procurement covers the VISDOMS-S Mission Phase A/B1. Based on the previous Space Based Optical Monitoring (SBOM) feasibility study, a mission concept using a small satellite and existing imager shall be further elaborated in a short Phase A. Suitable small platform candidates shall be further investigated in terms of its capacity and compliance towards the observational needs, the deorbiting requirements, and its capability to host the identified optical imager. The preliminary technical, engineering and quality assurance requirements for the Delta-Class mission shall be reviewed, agreed and consolidated as part of the Preliminary Requirements Review. The development approach shall be further elaborated with the objective to enable the establishment of the implementation and procurement plan. System optimisations based on previous flight experience that may lead to an improvement of the mission performance and its robustness by enhancing the existing equipment and optical imager may be considered for further elaboration during Phase B1.The Phase B1 industrial system study shall produce a preliminary design of the space and ground segment that shall include all elements for the mission definition, the spacecraft and the optical imager and the ground segment. The satellite design shall be matured, and a detailed accommodation study of the optical imager shall be performed. The design of the optical imager and potential modifications that may be required shall be addressed including the detector selection, readout electronics and the control and data processing unit. The technical requirements specifications of all major units shall be established, and the system requirements shall be consolidated and verified as far as possible by analysis. The study shall produce the necessary documentation for the System Requirements Review and confirm that the review objectives are achieved.

title: ESA BUSINESS INCUBATION CENTRE CYPRUS
description: The network of ESA Business Incubation Centers (ESA BICs) is the largest network of space incubators in Europe. The two main objectives of an ESA BICs are to:Support entrepreneurs with a space-based business idea;Create and grow clusters of space related start-ups across Europe. All the ESA BICs are managed by local incubators with experience in supporting start-ups. They have good connections with local industry, universities, research organisations, as well as relevant government agencies and investor communities. ESA BICs follow the ESA BIC Common Approach to business incubation. So far, the network of ESA BICs has supported more than 2000 start-ups. Cyprus recently completed the ESA-Cyprus Plan for European Cooperating State (PECS) programme and recognized that Spaceis not only an important domain of research and development, but one of the key pillars of modern economy. On the 17th of March 2026, Cyprus became an Associate Member of the European Space Agency (ESA). The seven-year agreement opens the way for Cyprus's participation in ESA's optional programmes. As such, the Cypriot delegation asked ESA to start the implementation of an ESA BIC in Cyprus, under the ACCESS optional programme, in order to promote and foster the creation of startups active in the Space sector.  The objective is to find and support 15 space-related incubatees over an active period of four years, with additional two years added to thecontract duration to support any incubatees until the end of the incubation program. Each selected incubatee shall be entitled to an incentive funding of at least 60kEUR.

title: ADVANCED SUSTAINABLE MANUFACTURING OF SPACE-QUALIFIED COMPONENTS FROM RECYCLED HIGH-VALUE FEEDSTOCK - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To identify, demonstrate, and implement recycling of high-value scrap into quality feedstock for additivemanufacturing of components for space applications.Description:As the demand for spacecraft, satellites and launch systems grows, so too does the consumption of criticalraw materials - many of which are finite, expensive and environmentally burdensome to extract. Recycling andreusing materials offer a strategic solution, reducing dependency on virgin resources, lowering carbonemissions and enhancing supply chain resilience. By integrating recycled materials into components, thespace sector can not only reduce its environmental footprint but also pioneer circular economy practices that will be essential for long-term sustainability - both on Earth and in future off-world manufacturing ecosystems.Furthermore, materials like titanium, aluminium and nickel alloys are in high demand in the space sector, yetthese materials are primarily imported from non-European sources. Developing local recycling solutions for high-value, critical materials is a vital step towards achieving European material self-sufficiency, especially in the current geopolitical and economic context. Potentially significant sources of scrap include machining waste (e.g. swarf, off cuts) and unused powder from additive manufacturing. Scrapped parts due to manufacturing defects are expected to be a secondary, less frequent, source but may become more relevant in the context of out-of-earth manufacturing. The space sector should also consider sourcing waste/scrap materials from other industries (e.g. aviation, automotive).The activity will start by identifying hot spots of high-value material scrap across European manufacturing(space and non-space). A hot spot in this context would be defined as materials with high volume of scrap,high material value/cost, raw material being sourced outside Europe, and high demand by the space industry.Selected scrap will then be processed into quality raw materials, tested, and used to produce and evaluate ademonstrator part to be defined based on a business case (e.g. bracket, fuel tank).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify sources of scrap material, material types relevant for space, and their possible use; down-selection of the most interesting cases (including economic, ecological and technical factors).- Develop processing route(s) for high-value material waste identified in the first task to transform into highquality raw materials for use as space hardware. This will most likely require dedicated alloy development to factor in what properties and quality can be realistically extracted from recycled materials.- Develop the advanced manufacturing process(es) for the use of "up-cycled" materials, considering theinfluence of impurities, potential development of detrimental phases, etc.- Test the produced material on a sample level (material characteristics, mechanical properties, etc.).- Design and manufacture a relevant spacedemonstrator part for subsequent testing to check compliance with relevant functional requirements.- Provide guidance on how to design components produced from recycled materials, seeking to identifypotential trade-offs between quality requirements, safety factors, cost and lead time.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report
